g12-economics-ue6-t1.overview: Concept of Poverty and Its Measurement sits inside Poverty and Inequality. Poverty and inequality are the focus of Unit 6 of Grade 12 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it defines poverty, its types, and how to measure it, including Sen’s approach. Then it explains income inequality and its measures. Next, it compares global and regional poverty and looks at women and poverty. Finally, it reviews poverty and inequality in Ethiopia and the role of indigenous knowledge. Students will also learn how poverty and inequality affect real-life communities.
objectives: Define poverty and explain how to measure it.
Explain income inequality and its measures.
Compare global, regional, and national poverty.
Identify the groups most affected by poverty.
Assess the role of indigenous knowledge in reducing poverty in Ethiopia.
g12-economics-ue6-t1.simple:
Concept of Poverty and Its Measurement in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, poverty and its types.
  • Then how to measure poverty.
  • Also Sen’s approach to poverty and wellbeing.
g12-economics-ue6-t1.detailed:
Concept of Poverty and Its Measurement — the essentials. First, poverty and its types. Then how to measure poverty. Also Sen’s approach to poverty and wellbeing.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Define poverty and explain how to measure it.
  • Explain income inequality and its measures.
  • Compare global, regional, and national poverty.
  • Identify the groups most affected by poverty.
  • Assess the role of indigenous knowledge in reducing poverty in Ethiopia.

keyTerms.term: Also Sen’s approach to poverty and wellbeing
